title: Resolve billing export discrepancies caused by usage-event duplicates and proration mismatch
creator: Maya Alvarez
description:
Summary: Multiple customer invoices and NetSuite export rows are showing cent-level mismatches and occasional duplicate line items. Root cause is twofold: (1) the usage ingestion pipeline sometimes creates duplicate usage_event rows when upstream rate-limit retries overlap with at-least-once delivery semantics, and (2) our internal proration math differs from Stripe's per-second proration handling leading to rounding drift that NetSuite later aggregates differently, producing invoice and AR reconciliation mismatches.

Investigation notes: Logs and export artifacts attached to this ticket show three classes of failures:
- Duplicate usage_event_id entries within a 2s window for the same customer+meter that were not deduplicated before billing aggregation. These generate duplicate invoice items when exports re-run.
- Proration mismatch where our prorated_amount_cents calculation uses day-based proportional split and rounds each line independently; Stripe calculates prorations with per-second weighting and preserves more precision before final invoice rounding. The difference is usually 1-3 cents but aggregates at scale.
- NetSuite import expects idempotent invoice line identifiers; when duplicate invoice_item_id rows are present we either create separate lines or NetSuite rejects and creates adjustments.

Proposed fix (MVP):
1) Dedupe at the billing aggregation layer using the canonical upstream usage_event_id and a 30s de-dupe window. Add a hard de-dupe step in the export job that collapses duplicates before summarization.
2) Replace internal proration routine with a Stripe-compatible implementation: compute prorated_amount in microcents using per-second weighting, carry extra precision through aggregation, then round once at the invoice line end. Store both computed_prorated_cents and stripe_proration_basis for audit.
3) Emit original_stripe_invoice_item_id and a stable export_row_id to NetSuite CSV so imports are idempotent and NetSuite adjustments map to source events.
4) Backfill: run a reprocess job for invoices from 2025-01-01 onward where exported totals != Stripe invoice totals and tag resubmits for accounting review.

Monitoring and validation:
- Add a daily reconciler job that compares Stripe invoice totals, internal aggregated totals, and NetSuite imported totals. Alert threshold: >$0.50 mismatch for any customer or >$100 aggregate for the day.
- Add metrics: billing.dedupe_rate, billing.proration_drift_cents_p50/p95, billing.reprocess_count. Dashboards: Billing > Reconciliation > Proration drift.

Risks and roll-out:
- Backfill reprocess may generate accounting noise; coordinate with Finance to surface resubmitted invoices as adjustments rather than new charges.
- Changing proration logic must be backwards compatible for signed historical invoices. Ensure we only apply Stripe-compatible proration for new invoices and use stored original values for audit.

Acceptance criteria:
- New export runs produce identical line item totals to Stripe invoices for a sample of 200 invoices (covering downgrades, mid-cycle upgrades, and multi-plan accounts).
- Duplicate usage_event-induced duplicate invoice items reduced to zero in new runs.
- NetSuite imports succeed idempotently for resubmitted CSVs and finance approves resubmit process.

Artifacts and links: PR - github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/2268 | Dashboard - grafana.redwood/internal/billing-recon | Finance runbook - drive.google.com/dl/finance-billing-recon-2025
